correctness.rationale: For m leaves, m+1 pairwise disjoint open intervals centered at i/m cannot all contain one leaf value; hence some boxed term has nonnegative minimum and their maximum is valid. On m+1 leaves assigning x=i/m, each box has a unique witness of value -1, making their maximum -1. Empty-infimum at leaves is 0 and all root valuations are bounded on the finite star. To prove minimality, any formula with at most m boxes has at most m syntactically outermost box occurrences evaluated at the root; keeping an attained infimum witness leaf for each and padding to m leaves preserves all such subformula values, including nested boxes whose values on leaves are 0. Leaf failures transfer verbatim. This proves all integers m≥1 and all real bounded valuations; checker independently reports 28170 finite tests but is not substituted for the proof.

originality.rationale: The motivating 2026 semantics and earlier 2018 real-valued modal proof techniques do not contain a checked assertion identifying the strict sequence of all finite rooted-star validity logics together with the sharp modal-occurrence complexity m+1. The constructed one-variable separator and matching lower bound add a precise frame-specific result. Earlier finite-star saturation results use nonadditive Gödel operations and do not imply a nonstabilizing Abelian hierarchy. Targeted semantic searches and the accessible literature found no dominating statement; this is a best-knowledge finding, not a universal uniqueness certificate.

value.rationale: The frame-theoretic problem asks how many accessible alternatives a real-valued modal logic can distinguish and how many modal observations are necessary. The result identifies a sharp, unbounded hierarchy for a natural nonreflexive star family, with explicit one-variable depth-one formulas and the optimal m+1 observation threshold. Contrasting the known finitely stabilizing Gödel fragments exposes a structural difference caused by additive pointed terms; a substantive all-m sharp separation and matching resource lower bound is not a routine single model check.
